title: Leverage Multipliers
hook: Working harder only adds. Leverage multiplies. I wish someone had told me that years ago.
statement: Each action should multiply your results, not just add to them. Use leverage instead of more effort.
explainer: Team, capital, systems, and audience all let one hour produce way more than one hour's worth. Without leverage, your income is capped by your calendar.
sop: List your five biggest time sinks from the last two weeks.
For each, pick a leverage point: team, capital, systems, or audience.
Before doing it yourself again, ask which one could take it.
Divide Output by Your Time on your biggest task and target the worst ratio.
Replace one recurring task with a delegated, automated, or templated version.
equation_example: Output $10,000, Your Time 20 hours. $10,000 ÷ 20 = 500, so $500 per hour. Higher means each hour produces more. Lower means you're trading hours for results at a flat rate that can't scale.
question: Write down one place you're adding more effort when you should be adding leverage.
closing_statement: Multiply your time before you spend more of it.
caption:
Principle Nº 171: Leverage Multipliers

Working harder only adds. Leverage multiplies. I wish someone had told me that years ago.

Each action should multiply your results, not just add to them. Use leverage instead of more effort.
